items.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 3 at 2:27PM EDT until October 4 at 4:00AM EDT by NWS Tallahassee FL
items.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Walton and Bay County Beaches.

* WHEN...Through late Saturday night.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
items.instruction:
Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

items.headline: Flood Watch issued October 3 at 2:24PM EDT until October 5 at 8:00AM EDT by NWS Tallahassee FL
items.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of Big Bend and Panhandle Florida, including the
following areas, in Big Bend Florida, Coastal Bay. In Panhandle
Florida, Central Walton, Coastal Gulf, Holmes, Inland Bay, Inland
Gulf, North Walton, South Walton and Washington.

* WHEN...Through Monday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Additional rainfall totals (beginning tonight through Monday) of
3 to 7 inches are forecast with the lower end of these ranges
more likely across out SW Georgia and Florida Big Bend counties
and the higher end of these totals more likely across the
Panhandle and into extreme southern portions of Alabama. Locally
higher amounts of 7 to 10 inches are possible along the Emerald
Coast by the time we get to early Monday morning.

- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
items.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.
